title: Gevini
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites the beginning of Shekalim, chapter 5: he was appointed in the Temple to proclaim, “Priests, rise for the service; Levites, to your platform; Israelites, to your stations.” King Agrippas heard his voice eight parasangs away. Hyman cites Mishnah Tamid 3:8 for the report that Gevini the herald was heard in Jericho, ten parasangs from Jerusalem. Yoma 20b says that Agrippas heard his voice three parasangs away (see Tosafot Yeshanim there) and gave him many gifts.

notes.text: The distances eight, ten and three parasangs are distinct statements in the source. The matching Mishnah is Tamid 3:8; the supplied מ״מ locator remains damaged.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier recorded matching Mishnah is Tamid3:8, beside supplied מ״מ; no chet/mem print history is proved. BEGINNING of Shekalim chapter5 is not silently made mishnah1. Eight parasangs for Agrippas, ten between Jericho and Jerusalem, and three in Yoma are three distinct claims and remain unchanged. The herald’s call names priests, Levites and Israelites separately; the Tosafot Yeshanim pointer remains Hyman’s citation, not a newly inspected commentary.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 300) gives מ״ח, identifying Mishnah Tamid 3:8, against מ״מ in the supplied transcription. The Mishnah names the herald and says he was heard in Jericho. Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 5:1:14 gives eight parasangs and gifts, while Yoma 20b gives three and separately states the ten-parasang distance in its comparison with the High Priest. Tosafot Yeshanim there records several ways of reading the accounts, including the view that they disagree.
